correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), the coordinate vectors in \(\ell_{p_n}^{2}\) are exactly Birkhoff--James orthogonal and have both endpoint norms \(2^{1/p_n}\). Since \(p_n\downarrow1\), these values increase to \(2\), forcing \(J_B^0(X)=J(X)=2\); monotonicity of the approximate profile then gives \(J_B^{\varepsilon}(X)=2\) for every \(0\le\varepsilon<1\). The \(\ell_2\)-sum is reflexive and strictly convex, and strict convexity makes simultaneous equalities \(\|x+y\|=\|x-y\|=2\) impossible for unit vectors, so the supremum is not attained. Every inference is exact and infinite-dimensional; no computation or finite sample is used as a proof.

value.rationale: The finding isolates a structural boundary of a newly introduced invariant rather than adding a routine numerical example. It shows that \(\sigma_B(X)=0\) need not encode an attained extremal configuration: even reflexivity and strict convexity allow the saturation to be purely asymptotic. This directly explains why the source's finite-dimensional maximum formula cannot be transferred verbatim to infinite dimensions and gives a concrete test example for future extensions of the theory.
